CheriBSD's revocation sweeps capabilities to freed heap memory, so the stale pointer SHOULD be revoked and the probe fault -- but only if the sweep has run between the free and the access. The reduction frees and re-allocates immediately, which is the case least favourable to revocation, so a clean reading here is about sweep TIMING and not about the defect. That must be read in-guest before it is called either way.

title: an interior pointer into a freed pass struct was dereferenced to read a field
object: a SwsOpPass from av_mallocz, with `comp` an interior pointer at &p->comp
lifetime_ender: av_free(p), the pass struct, on the path that hands its compiled parts onward
shape: an interior pointer into a freed object, used after the object was freed
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, with no pool or refstruct layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is `comp->backend->flags`, where comp points INSIDE the freed p.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libswscale/ops_dispatch.c reads `c.backend->flags`. The stale form, `comp->backend->flags`, is at 716d2a47c565^ and is absent from the pin.
nested_why: the object came straight from av_malloc/av_mallocz/av_malloc_array/av_realloc -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool, AVRefStructPool or other recycling layer between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../pool-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the stale pointer is not the one that was freed -- it is an INTERIOR pointer into the same allocation, which is why no amount of nulling the outer pointer would have helped and why the fix reads from the local copy `c` instead. A bounds-only configuration cannot see this at all: the address is in bounds of whatever now occupies the chunk.
